structured_output.conclusion: On 20 May 2024 the court entered a $38,595,023 judgment against Akoustis Technologies, Inc. in favour of Qorvo, Inc. It is made up of $31,315,215 in unjust-enrichment damages, $7,000,000 in exemplary damages and $279,808 in patent damages. It had not been paid, and no admissible order sets a date to pay, post a bond or stay it. Motions filed on 17 June 2024 are pending, with briefing closing on 8 August 2024. Akoustis asks for a new trial or a cut in the $31.3M part to $305,000. Qorvo asks for trebling to $93,945,645 in total compensatory damages, $12,116,123.30 in fees, and interest (amount sealed). Akoustis says the damages would exceed its liquid assets. It reported about $15.2M of cash at 31 March 2024 and substantial doubt about continuing as a going concern. It says that without new financing it must cut back or stop operations and/or seek bankruptcy protection. The judgment is modelled as a possible cash outflow of Akoustis with an unknown date (eff_006; dispute_001). The judgment is larger than the $10.0M threshold in the $44.0M 6.0% convertible notes. If a final judgment stays unpaid or unstayed for 60 days after notice from the trustee or holders of 25% of the notes, those holders can declare the notes, due June 2027, immediately due (eff_009; financing_001). Linking the judgment to this clause applies the notes' own terms to the court's figure; when the judgment counts as final is unknown. Akoustis also must get its share price back above Nasdaq's $1.00 minimum by 21 October 2024, and delisting is a separate default on the notes. Qorvo's request to bar sales of the products that infringe its two patents has not been decided. Akoustis says its redesigned XBAW filters are not affected.
